Liveness/readiness probe; exempt from auth, and skipped at the OIDC gate
so an external observer can read which release serves without a credential.

The MCP HTTP Basic credential (base64 of user:password) for the in-app
"Connect agent" one-liner.

Reachable only by an already-authenticated caller: under scope=mcp the
oauth2-proxy in front admits only a logged-in, allowlisted human; under
scope=all the Basic gate covers it. Answers 503 when the credential is unset,
mirroring the fail-closed auth posture (there is nothing to hand out).

AppResponse.title: AppResponse
AppResponse.description:
A manifest entry joined with its team-folder facts, when onboarded.

``name`` and ``repo`` are two facts: the name keys everything the platform
renders (namespace, hostname, chart, packages), the repo names where the
code lives. ``repo`` is always resolved - the declared value, else the name
- so a caller never re-derives the default, and it is present even for an
app declared but not yet onboarded, where ``manifest`` (and so
``manifest.repo_url``) is still None.

AppStatusResponse.title: AppStatusResponse
AppStatusResponse.description:
The delivery evidence chain of one app, typed link by link.

``stage`` is one of not_onboarded, pr_open, awaiting_first_artifacts,
promoted, serving; serving requires promotion, sync and probe links ok.
``sync`` compares the primary Application applied revision and operation
with the requested deploy head. ``probe`` retains HTTP and workload facts;
unknown workload proof keeps it skipped. ``chart`` compares effective
published renders and is advisory.
``summary`` names the stage and the first link that is not ok, in chain
order. ``grant_drift`` reports whether each capability grant on the branch
still matches what its canonical template renders, which is advisory: it
names a hand edit rather than refusing anything.
``credentials`` reports whether every platform-minted credential
the app's chart names has the install grant that mints it; it sits outside
the stage derivation, explaining a hostname that does not answer.
``smoke`` reports the app's in-cluster deployed-smoke verdict, read off
the platform's smoke reporter at the docs host (ADR-047); advisory, and
skipped for an app that has not adopted the contract.

CancelOnboardingRequest.title: CancelOnboardingRequest
CancelOnboardingRequest.description:
The branch to clear off the remote.

Named in full (``onboard/<app>``, ``onboard/<app>-db``,
``offboard/<app>``, ``reconcile/<app>``, ``settings/<key>``), exactly as
the refusal that blocked the re-run reported it.

CancelledChangeResponse.title: CancelledChangeResponse
CancelledChangeResponse.description:
What the cancel found and what it removed.

``deleted`` is false when the remote already carried no such branch: the
verb is idempotent, so a repeat reports a clear remote rather than
failing. ``prs`` carries every pull request that ever referenced the
branch, and is empty for the orphan case the verb exists for.

ClaimResponse.title: ClaimResponse
ClaimResponse.description: One intent claim the conformance suite attests.

ConformanceReportResponse.title: ConformanceReportResponse
ConformanceReportResponse.description: Outcome of the platform's conformance suite returned over HTTP.

CreateAppRepoRequest.title: CreateAppRepoRequest
CreateAppRepoRequest.description:
The facts a walking-skeleton repo is rendered from.

``name`` is the fleet name: the chart, the GHCR package prefix, and later
the namespace and hostname. ``repo`` is the repository to create it in,
a separate fact (INT-SKELETON-001) that defaults to the name - an
organisation shared with other work prefixes its repositories while its
apps keep their own names, and without this the two could only ever be the
same string. ``display_name`` and ``description`` seed the landing page,
the docs site, and the README, and are re-declared to the onboarding later
(the manifest stays the single source of the tile facts).

OffboardAppRequest.title: OffboardAppRequest
OffboardAppRequest.description:
The one fact an offboarding needs: which app to retire.

The removal is derived from the record itself (the manifest entry and
whatever the teams/<app>/ folder holds), so nothing else is declared
here. The merge also prunes the app's namespace, deleting every volume
its own chart claims, with its data on a Delete reclaim policy, so those
volumes are copied out before the call. Stateful grants are never
dropped by the offboarding: the pull request enumerates them for an
explicit disposition decision.

OnboardAppRequest.title: OnboardAppRequest
OnboardAppRequest.description:
The operator-facing facts an app onboarding needs.

``role`` is the manifest list the entry lands in (ADR-032): ``parts`` for
the apps the Foundry depends on, ``output`` (the default) for the apps it
built and runs. ``image_components`` names the app's released images when
there is more than one (e.g. ``["server", "client", "docs"]``): the
Application then watches one GHCR package per component
(``<name>-<component>``) and writes ``<name>.images.<component>.tag``;
empty means the single-image shape (package ``<name>``,
``<name>.image.tag``). ``repo`` is the app's repository under the org, the
one thing the rendered Application's ``repoURL`` points at; empty defaults
to ``name``, the same string for most apps. ``name`` is the fleet name
(namespace, hostname label, chart, GHCR packages), so an app whose
repository is named differently from itself names both.
``allow_bootstrap`` waives the strict admission on
skipped app-side conformance legs (the deliberate walking-skeleton
bootstrap, recorded in the PR body).

OnboardDatabaseRequest.title: OnboardDatabaseRequest
OnboardDatabaseRequest.description:
The facts a database grant needs: whose it is, and whether skipped
app-side conformance legs are waived (the walking-skeleton bootstrap).

OnboardEventsRequest.title: OnboardEventsRequest
OnboardEventsRequest.description:
The facts an events grant needs: whose it is, which REF-Events domains it
may publish under, and whether skipped app-side conformance legs are waived
(the walking-skeleton bootstrap).

``domains`` has no default. Publishing is owned per domain, so a grant that
named none would admit a reader while looking like a producer grant, and one
defaulting to the app's own name would coin a domain the type registry never
agreed to.

OnboardIdentityRequest.title: OnboardIdentityRequest
OnboardIdentityRequest.description:
The facts a realm grant needs: whose it is, and whether skipped
app-side conformance legs are waived (the walking-skeleton bootstrap).

OnboardingResultResponse.title: OnboardingResultResponse
OnboardingResultResponse.description: What an onboarding changed, what the gates said, and where it went.

PlatformSettingResponse.title: PlatformSettingResponse
PlatformSettingResponse.description:
One platform knob as the install's deploy branch currently has it.

`value` is what the install pins, or null when it pins nothing; `default`
is the chart's fallback; `effective` is what the component runs with. The
three are reported separately so a caller can tell "explicitly set to 30
days" from "inherits 30 days", which differ the moment the chart's default
moves.

PrInfoResponse.title: PrInfoResponse
PrInfoResponse.description:
Identity and state of one onboarding pull request.

``merged`` is the admission signal an onboarding run polls for: only
``merged: true`` means the platform repo's CI admitted the app (ADR-036);
a closed-not-merged PR is an abandonment.

ReconcileAppRequest.title: ReconcileAppRequest
ReconcileAppRequest.description:
The fresh declaration a reconcile re-renders the team folder against.

``image_components`` is the accountable re-declaration of the app's
released images (empty means the single-image shape), the one input that
usually motivates the reconcile; ``description`` refreshes the manifest's
tile description when given (empty keeps the current one); ``repo``
overrides the repository the Application points at and the manifest
entry records (empty keeps the entry's, else the Application's).
Display, icon, role, and the mcp flag are read from the existing manifest
entry: reconcile repairs the rendered folder, it does not rebrand the app.

ReconcileIdentityRequest.title: ReconcileIdentityRequest
ReconcileIdentityRequest.description:
The facts a realm re-render needs: whose realm, and whether skipped
app-side conformance legs are waived (the walking-skeleton bootstrap).

Nothing else is taken: the declaration a re-render applies is the install's
own (``defaultBrokers`` and the login theme on its deploy branch), never a
caller's, so the realm can only ever be brought to what the branch says.

RefreshResponse.title: RefreshResponse
RefreshResponse.description: Acknowledgement that the checkout was reconciled with upstream.

RepoScaffoldResponse.title: RepoScaffoldResponse
RepoScaffoldResponse.description: The created repository and the onboarding declaration it takes.

StatusLinkResponse.title: StatusLinkResponse
StatusLinkResponse.description:
One link of the delivery evidence chain: its verdict and detail.

``status`` is ok, failed, or skipped; a skipped link's detail always
names the reason it could not be evaluated.

TeamManifestResponse.title: TeamManifestResponse
TeamManifestResponse.description: The onboarding facts one team manifest fixes.

TestResultResponse.title: TestResultResponse
TestResultResponse.description:
One pytest node id, its verdict, and what the node id cannot say.

``detail`` names the concrete artifact a row judged (the repository that
would not answer, say); rows whose node id is self-explanatory leave it
empty.

UpdateSettingRequest.title: UpdateSettingRequest
UpdateSettingRequest.description:
The new value for the knob named in the path.

Shape only here: what counts as a valid value is the knob's own unit
(a duration for the retention horizons), judged in the domain, so the rule
lives with the registry that declares the unit rather than being restated
per transport.
